correctness.rationale: The minimal prefix DFA and all state transitions are explicitly defined. The proof partitions all nonidentity idempotents by initial letter run into disjoint killed-domain classes and proves both realizability and exhaustiveness, including separate r=1 and s=1 cases. It counts these classes by finite sums and proves the rank bound. Two independent standard-library enumerators each exhaust all transition monoids for 1<=r,s<=10; the second verifies exact set equality with the four-family retraction catalogue for every pair. Finite checks corroborate but are not substituted for the all-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: A direct same-object published theorem from 2013 already counts the whole syntactic semigroup, but its stated output and proof do not provide the idempotence law or explicit rank-two retractions. A 2017 broader semigroup extremal bound concerns other witness monoids, while the 2023 motivating work treats learning of monoids and not two-run factor-idempotent classification. Actual indexed-record and literature searches revealed no covering claim. An unindexed equivalent remains possible; absence of a search hit is not treated as a proof of novelty.

value.rationale: Idempotents describe precisely the stable (one-repeat) transformations of a syntactic monoid. The family is a canonical binary two-run pattern-recognition language with a known total syntactic complexity, yet its idempotent retraction geometry is not supplied by total-size results. The exact count, nonidentity rank-two structure and asymptotic 1/2-versus-3/5 density contrast are intrinsic, fully classified semigroup invariants useful as transparent structural benchmarks. No unproved downstream learning-speed guarantee is asserted.
